# Charlotte (01, engineer) — BAD-076

## Brief
Stop `next dev` from rewriting `admin/CLAUDE.md`.

## The bug

Next 16 ships `admin/node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. When
`next dev` starts and detects an AI coding agent, `writeAgentFiles()` upserts a managed
block between `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` and `<!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->`
into `AGENTS.md` if one exists, else into `CLAUDE.md`. `admin/` has no `AGENTS.md`, so it
lands in `admin/CLAUDE.md` — a ten-line append, and the file is otherwise hand-written
project guidance.

The result: anyone who follows `admin/README.md:208` (`cd admin && npm install && npm run
seed && npm run dev`) ends up with ` M admin/CLAUDE.md` in their diff, unrelated to their
work. It has ridden along into open PRs twice already (the worktrees for BAD-053 PR 1 and
BAD-054 PR 2); a spudagent cannot revert it, because the file is outside its deliverable
globs and Law 7 forbids `git restore`. The block's own text says removing it from a diff
only re-creates the change.

## The decision (already made — implement it, do not re-litigate)

Turn the generator off with `agentRules: false` in `admin/next.config.mjs`, and move the
one piece of real advice the block carries into `admin/CLAUDE.md` in the repo's own words,
where nothing rewrites it.

Why this and not the two alternatives the ticket listed:

- *Committing the block* is the generator's own suggestion, and it leaves the tree clean
  only until a Next upgrade edits the block text — then the next `npm run dev` dirties the
  file again. It trades a permanent fix for a recurring one.
- *Adding `admin/AGENTS.md`* moves the churn to a different file instead of ending it, and
  puts a second agent-guidance file in a directory that already has a careful one.

`agentRules` is a real top-level config option in the version we run (`next` `^16.3.4`);
it is in the schema at `admin/node_modules/next/dist/server/config-schema.js:496` and typed
at `config-shared.d.ts:1574`. Confirm that yourself before relying on it.

## What to build

1. **`admin/next.config.mjs`** — add `agentRules: false` with a comment explaining what it
   turns off and why. Match the file's established voice: its comments are long, specific,
   and explain the failure they prevent rather than restating the option name. Say that
   `next dev` otherwise appends a managed block to `CLAUDE.md` (there is no `AGENTS.md`
   here), that it re-adds it on every run so removing it from a diff does not help, and
   that the advice it carries is stated in `admin/CLAUDE.md` instead. Name the generator's
   path so the next person can check it. Put it somewhere sensible among the existing keys.

2. **`admin/CLAUDE.md`** — add a short passage carrying the block's substance in the file's
   own voice: this is Next 16, its APIs and conventions differ from what a model's training
   data holds, and the authoritative reference is the version-matched docs bundled at
   `admin/node_modules/next/dist/docs/` — read the relevant guide there before writing Next
   code. Say the generated block is switched off in `next.config.mjs` and why, so nobody
   re-enables it or wonders where it went.

   Read the file first and place it where it belongs. It is a long, carefully written
   document; match its register and do not restructure it. Two to eight lines is the right
   size — this is a pointer, not an essay. Do not touch anything else in it.

## Verify

`.claude/skills/implementing-changes` owns what proves a change here — read it first and
follow its tier for this kind of change. At minimum, prove the actual bug is gone:

1. `git status --porcelain` — confirm clean before you start (after your two edits, confirm
   only those two files are modified).
2. `cd admin && npm install` if `admin/node_modules` is missing in this worktree.
3. Run the dev server the way `admin/README.md` tells a person to: `npm run dev` from
   `admin/`. Give it enough time to boot and print its startup banner, then stop it. Run it
   in the background and poll rather than blocking your turn on it.
4. `git status --porcelain` again — `admin/CLAUDE.md` must show only *your* edit, with no
   `nextjs-agent-rules` markers anywhere: `grep -rn 'nextjs-agent-rules' admin/` should find
   nothing outside `node_modules/`. Also confirm no `admin/AGENTS.md` was scaffolded.
5. Run it a second time and check again — the first run proves the option is read, the
   second proves it is not a one-shot.
6. Confirm the config still parses for a build path, not just dev: `npm run lint` in
   `admin/` at minimum. A full `npm run build` is better if it is not prohibitively slow
   here; say which you ran.

If `agentRules: false` turns out not to suppress the write in this version, stop and
`member block` with what you observed — do not fall back to committing the block on your
own judgment.
